paper_title: MMAR A Challenging Benchmark for Deep Reasoning in Speech, Audio,   Music, and Their Mix
caption: Error distribution in Audio-Reasoner.
model_annotation: The pie chart illustrates the error distribution in the Audio-Reasoner model as reported in the paper “MMAR: A Challenging Benchmark for Deep Reasoning in Speech, Audio, Music, and Their Mix.” It is divided into seven distinct categories, each represented by a differently colored segment and labeled with its corresponding percentage. The largest segment, colored in light purple, represents “Perceptual Error” at 37%. The second largest, in medium purple, is “Reasoning Error” at 20%. Following that, “Correct Answer but Wrong Choice” accounts for 15% (darker purple), and “Repeat Thinking and No Answer” makes up 12% (light blue). Smaller segments include “Lack of Knowledge” at 9% (sky blue), “Choice Format Error” at 4% (very light cyan), and “Wrong Understanding of Instruction” at 3% (pale mint green). Arrows point from the labels to their respective slices, and percentage values are clearly displayed within each segment. The chart visually emphasizes the dominance of perceptual and reasoning errors over other categories, with the remaining error types collectively constituting less than one-third of the total.
